Written d: 'a voiced interdental fricative'; Sonsorolese d is always Hatohobeian s (p. 21).

Written gl: 'a stop that is made by raising the tongue-root to the velum as in [g] ... while curving down the sides of the tongue to allow a lateral release'; analysed as a lateralized velar [gˡ], not a velarized lateral [ɫ], because it is a stop and corresponds to the Hatohobeian velar fricative h (maglam : maham 'moon') (pp. 21-22). Charted as a fricative in the 'lateralized velar' column (Table 10, p. 22), and Capell, as she cites him, calls it a lateral velar consonant (p. 9). Entered as a lateral velar (decision vandenberg2014-symbols).
